results.summary: AI's shift from training to inference is driving rapid and accelerating growth in memory demand, particularly HBM.
results.quote: rapid growth in memory demand driven by AI's shift from training to inference
results.evidence: The transcript window explicitly names 'Gavin Baker, CIO and Managing Partner of Atreides Management' as the speaker sharing these insights at the 2025 Sohn Montreal Conference, and a self-referential turn confirms Baker thanked the Sohn Foundation and set the conversational tone.

results.summary: SK Hynix is the dominant HBM supplier and offers ~3x upside as the primary beneficiary of AI inference-driven memory demand.
results.quote: 3X Upside Riding the AI Inference Wave with a Dominant HBM Supplier
results.evidence: The article headline and body directly attribute the '3X Upside' HBM thesis to Gavin Baker of Atreides Management presenting at Sohn Montreal 2025, with no other speaker indicated.

results.summary: Reasoning models (advanced inference-time compute scaling) are a structural catalyst for HBM demand growth beyond what consensus expects.
results.quote: advancements in reasoning models and high-bandwidth memory are reshaping the semiconductor landscape
results.evidence: The same turn explicitly attributes the reasoning-models-and-HBM insight to Gavin Baker by name, noting his two decades of technology investing experience as context for the claim.
